problem: Social navigation planners reduce humans to points or circles and discard body-language cues such as pose, gait and orientation. Pose-aware trajectory predictors are decoupled from planning and need skeleton tracking that robots often cannot run at deployment.
motivation: Humans read whole-body cues to anticipate others' motion, but onboard robots lack the sensors or compute to track skeletons in real time. Privileged skeletal information available at training time could be distilled into a vision-only policy that infers these cues implicitly.
key_idea: Train a skeleton-aware Oracle Teacher transformer for goal-conditioned robot trajectory planning, then distill its latent social representation into a lightweight RGB-only Student via feature alignment plus trajectory imitation.
insight: Skeleton-aware teacher latents transfer to an RGB-only student: distilling from the full teacher gives lower ADE/FDE than distilling from a vision-only teacher (0.578/1.064 vs 0.585/1.078), though the gap is modest and AOE is marginally worse (0.159 vs 0.157). Adding an auxiliary human-trajectory-prediction head to the teacher hurts performance by about 2.8% on average, suggesting conflicting gradients between forecasting and planning. The end-to-end approach also beats a decoupled HST+MPC pipeline that uses the same keypoints.
method: Oracle Teacher inputs: egocentric RGB (frozen DINOv3, all tokens), robot state history via MLP, goal token, and per-human privileged state (30 3D keypoints from SAM3DBody + ByteTrack, plus relative 2D position and facing direction) for up to M=10 humans.

Body-Part-Aware Human Encoder: splits keypoints into Head/Torso/Arms/Legs, applies part-specific MLPs and learnable part-type embeddings, concatenates position and facing direction, and fuses them with an MLP into one human token per human per timestep.

Hierarchical Robot-Centric Fusion: (1) HST-style temporal and social attention extended with bidirectional robot-human attention; (2) time-aligned cross-attention from robot tokens to visual tokens; (3) self-attention over robot tokens plus goal token.

Trajectory Head: 4-layer MLP on the flattened (T+1)·D tokens. The third layer output Z_teacher is the distillation target, and the fourth layer outputs 12 (x,y) waypoints. The Teacher is trained with an MSE loss.

Sensorimotor Student: lightweight trainable CNN (ResNet) encoder for images, a goal encoder, and a scaled-down transformer with a learnable CLS token. Only the CLS token goes through a projector and an MLP head, forcing compression into a compact belief state.
Distillation objective: L_total = L_traj (MSE to ground truth) + λ·L_feat (MSE between projected student CLS and frozen teacher Z_teacher). At test time the Student uses only RGB and the goal.

setting.backbone: Teacher: frozen DINOv3 + transformer fusion (trained from scratch); Student: ResNet + small transformer (trained via distillation)
setting.training_data: SCAND filtered to about 12,000 training samples (2,000 test); an OOD set of about 2,000 teleoperated AgileX Scout Mini samples used only for evaluation; skeletal labels generated offline with SAM3DBody + ByteTrack
setting.observation: Student: egocentric monocular RGB history (6 frames at 4 Hz) plus a local goal position; Teacher additionally gets 3D skeletal keypoints, human positions/facing, and robot state history
setting.action_space: Predicted future 2D waypoint trajectory (12 steps, about 3 s)
setting.simulator: none; offline datasets (SCAND, own OOD set) and a real robot
setting.privileged: Teacher only, at training time: skeletal keypoints, human positions and facing direction. The Student uses none at test time.

numbers.eval_set_note: about 2,000 held-out SCAND samples; the text is ambiguous about whether Table 1 covers SCAND test or the OOD set
numbers.backbone: ResNet student distilled from DINOv3-based Oracle Teacher
numbers.extra: Goal given as a position 15 m ahead; the baselines ViNT, NoMaD and GNM use goal images

results: HumAIN reaches ADE 0.578 m, FDE 1.064 m and AOE 0.159 rad. Against the strongest baseline on each metric this is a 23.2% ADE, 14.2% FDE and 21.7% AOE reduction (about 29.8% average gain claimed), beating GNM/ViNT and HST+MPC. Real-robot tests on a Jackal show qualitatively human-aware yielding behavior.
limitations: Evaluation uses displacement error against teleoperated ground truth rather than closed-loop social metrics, and real-robot results are only qualitative
Not robust enough for open-world deployment: crowded scenes, occlusions and multiple interacting pedestrians remain difficult
Limited by dataset size and diversity (SCAND teleoperation biases); the benefit of skeletal privileged information is modest in the ablation
